extracted.intended_audience: students and researchers in topology (advanced undergraduates, graduate students, and professional mathematicians)
extracted.subtask_description: Annotated, curated list of recommended books across topology subfields (introductory through advanced), with short evaluations about level, style, coverage, availability, and usefulness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Readability / Expository quality
rubrics_metrics.description: How pleasant and accessible the exposition is to read.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples from the list: 'A pleasure to read.'; 'Quite elementary and accessible.'; 'Highly readable and highly recommended.' Indicates preference for clear, engaging exposition rather than dry/pedestrian treatments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Level / Prerequisites / Target audience
rubrics_metrics.description: The mathematical maturity and prerequisites required (elementary, beginner, advanced, research-level).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The list explicitly ranges 'from elementary to advanced' and annotates books as 'elementary and accessible', 'for a beginner', 'more advanced', or 'technical handbook'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage / Scope of topics
rubrics_metrics.description: Which parts of topology the book treats and how comprehensively (introductory overview vs focused topic vs broad survey).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries note coverage such as 'Includes basics on smooth manifolds, and even some point-set topology', 'A whole book on this classic theorem and its many varied applications', or 'A small fraction of the theory can be found in...'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perspective / Conceptual viewpoint
rubrics_metrics.description: The viewpoint or approach taken (geometric, differential-forms, spectral-sequence-focused, PL, surgery, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'Develops algebraic topology from the point of view of differential forms.'; books are grouped by viewpoints like differential forms, K-theory, PL topology, geometric vs classical/topological approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suitability as a textbook vs reference/handbook
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the book is intended as a pedagogical textbook, a reference, or a technical handbook.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annotations distinguish 'textbook exposition is still lacking', 'A technical handbook, not as user-friendly', 'A fine reference book on point-set topology' and 'standard reference'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of proofs, exercises, and level of detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether proofs are included or left as exercises; how detailed or skeletal the treatment is.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'Essentially just an outline with proofs left as exercises, but with many insightful comments.'; also notes 'only 65 pages, so only a small amount of material is covered'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability / In-print status and price
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the book is in print, out of print (OP), and its price (noting variability and inflation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author gave 2003 prices and marks many entries '[OP]'; comments: 'The number of topology books has been increasing... For the books that were still in print in 2003 I gave the price... wide variation in prices... ridiculously inflated the prices from some publishers are.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Free online availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the book (or an unfinished/online version) is available for free download.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marked explicitly, e.g. 'Free electronic version available at http://www.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher' and 'Unfinished book available online at ...'; page notes when books are available for free downloading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Usefulness for learning specific techniques or computations
rubrics_metrics.description: How useful the book is for calculations, specific techniques (spectral sequences, cobordism calculations), or as a practical toolbox.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'The first 100 pages ... give a nice overview' (surgery); 'An older book emphasizing the calculations of the coeﬃcient rings of various forms of cobordism.'; 'A technical handbook' and 'Includes a very nice introduction to spectral sequences.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Big-picture / conceptual intuition
rubrics_metrics.description: How well the book conveys the overall picture, motivation, and intuition of the subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'Good for getting the big picture.'; 'Emphasizes ideas and intuition.'; recommendations highlight books that give the 'big picture' vs purely technical presentations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical / classical value
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the book is included primarily for historical interest or because it is a classic foundational text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The list includes 'classics' and notes 'included in this list mainly for their historical interest' (e.g., Eilenberg–Steenrod, Spanier, Steenrod's fiber bundles).

rubrics_metrics.name: Currency / coverage of recent developments
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the book reflects modern developments or is out of date for current approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments such as 'The newer generalizations haven't yet filtered down to the textbook level' and inclusion of newer surveys vs older classical texts; some topics lack a good modern textbook per the author.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specialization / depth in advanced topics
rubrics_metrics.description: The depth and specialization level for advanced/special topics (elliptic cohomology, stable homotopy, localization, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple advanced titles are listed with annotations like 'one of the few textbook sources for the slowly emerging and potentially very important topic of elliptic cohomology' and listings of monographs and research-level texts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliability / presence of errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the book is technically reliable or contains notable errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'A technical handbook, not as user-friendly as one might wish, and with some glaring errors, but included here in the absence of other sources.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation aids: pictures, clarity of exposition, and pedagogy
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality of illustrations, diagrams, and pedagogical devices (pictures, examples) that help accessibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit in comments like 'noteworthy for its readability and nice pictures' (Rolfsen) and emphasis on books that 'emphasize ideas and intuition.'
